title: Tire width to rim internal width helper
description: Choose a tire size or rim inner width to automatically see one best width. A separate card combines the normal fitment range with its standards and manufacturer references. Best results for tires up to 30 mm include aero matching.

tireWidthPresetInchSection: Inch markings (common mountain and off-road labels)

innerWidthForStatusNote: Choose your current rim width or preview another size. The result and section diagram below update from this selection.
rimSystemHelpTitle: What is the difference between hooked and hookless rims?
rimSystemHelpIntro: Hooked and hookless describe the rim sidewall shape that retains the tire bead. They are a separate compatibility question from tubeless or inner-tube use.
rimSystemHelpHookedDiagram: Cross-section photo of a hooked rim with a bead hook
rimSystemHelpHookedBody: The inner sidewall has a bead hook that gives the bead mechanical retention when inflated. It may support a tire with an inner tube or a tubeless tire, but the exact rim and tire specifications still decide compatibility.
rimSystemHelpHooklessDiagram: Cross-section photo of a hookless rim with a straight sidewall
rimSystemHelpHooklessBody: The straight sidewall has no bead hook, so retention depends on precise bead-seat dimensions and the tire bead. Use only a tire explicitly marked as TSS/Hookless compatible; adding an inner tube does not make an ordinary clincher automatically compatible.
rimSystemHelpUseTitle: How should you read this by riding category?
rimSystemHelpUseBody: Hookless is common in modern mountain-bike tubeless systems and is widely used for Gravel. Road riding is not limited to hooked rims: Zipp 303 and ENVE SES include road hookless products. Hooked rims also remain common in many road, commuter, touring, and older systems, so confirm the exact model.
rimSystemHelpSafety: Do not infer compatibility from “road” or “mountain” alone. Confirm the rim’s TSS/TC construction, the tire’s compatibility marking, and the pressure and installation limits from the rim, tire, and wheelset manufacturers.

outOfRange: This width is outside the current engineering model. Check the exact tire and rim manufacturer specifications.
noPublishedBracket: The current engineering model has no window for this width. Check the exact tire and rim manufacturer specifications.
engineeringReferenceNote: This result is inside the engineering reference window, not certification for a specific tire, rim, or wheelset model.
rimOuterWidthEstimateLabel: Estimated rim outer width (about {wallThickness} mm per side):
physicsNote: The selected millimetre width is used directly as the tire width; it is not widened again for rim inner width. Estimated rim outer width = inner width + 2 × side-wall thickness (about 3 mm); the aero relationship is tire width ≈ rim outer width × 1.05, so known-tire mode derives the target rim outer width as tire width ÷ 1.05. Actual rim outer width varies by profile and widest point, so use the maker's specification. These are estimates, not measured dimensions or safety limits.
normalFitmentPhysicsNote: Normal ranges are looked up in the ISO 5775-1:2023 width table. The 105% aero calculation is not used above 30C. Confirm exact product installation approval with the makers.
requestError: Calculation results are temporarily unavailable. Please try again.

layered.frameClearanceNote: Compare your tire model's maximum width, diameter and shoulder diameter in the Schwalbe tables with the available frame, fork and chainstay space. Measure the fitted tire to confirm its actual dimensions.
layered.pairing: Rim inner width {rimWidth} mm · tire width {tireWidth} mm
layered.aeroSelectionNote: Selected against the 105% geometric target and normal fitment range; this is not installation approval for a specific product.
layered.wideSelectionNote: Size guidance is matched automatically to the known dimensions to select one best width. The full fitment range is shown in the card below.
layered.noBestNote: No size meets the recommendation conditions for this use. Normal reference ranges remain below.
layered.noFatBestNote: There is no reviewed Fat recommendation for this size. Consult the normal reference range below and confirm the specific rim and tire models.
layered.normalNote: This is the width-pairing range. Related standards and manufacturer guidance are listed below in this card.
layered.standardRole: ISO and ETRTO define normal dimensional fitment ranges. The displayed range has not yet been verified against the original tables and must not be read as their table result.
layered.standardRangeRole: This card's normal fitment range comes from the table's nominal tire and rim widths. The best-width card above provides a separate recommendation.
layered.manufacturerRole: Manufacturer guidance adds size suggestions for the relevant rim. General fitment ranges remain governed by the standards tables.
layered.outerWidthAssumption: About 3 mm per side is an outer-width estimate. Use the exact rim specification; wide-tire selection does not use this wall-thickness assumption.
layered.noPressureNote: No universal pressure limit is supplied. Follow the exact rim and tire specifications.

enteredReasons.below_minimum: The entered tire is below the normal fitment minimum of {minimum} mm.
enteredReasons.above_maximum: The entered tire exceeds the normal fitment maximum of {maximum} mm.
enteredReasons.recommended_window: The entered pairing is inside the recommended window for this use; the single recommendation remains above.
enteredReasons.reference_window: The entered pairing is inside the normal reference range, outside the recommended window.
enteredReasons.no_recommended_window: The entered pairing is inside the normal reference range; size-optimization guidance is unavailable for this use.
enteredReasons.transitional_rim: This is a transitional reference rim size, not a best-pairing selection.
